stem:
The diagram shows lines $PQ$ and $RS$ cut by transversal $AC$. Triangles $PAC$ and $RCA$ are congruent, and that congruence makes a pair of alternate interior angles equal.

Which claim correctly concludes that $PQ \parallel RS$?

options.text: Because the congruent triangles give equal alternate interior angles for transversal $AC$, lines $PQ$ and $RS$ are parallel.
Report the words alternate interior angles as the names of lines $PQ$ and $RS$.
The triangles are congruent, so $PQ \parallel RS$ even when no alternate interior angles are used.
Equal side lengths in the triangles alone prove $PQ \parallel RS$, with no equal alternate interior angles needed.

teacher.key_rationale: Congruence yields equal alternate interior angles on transversal AC, which forces PQ ∥ RS. Naming the angle type as the lines, dropping the alternate-interior step, or stretching side-length equality to a parallel proof all miss the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote the source bolt-triangle figure as lines PQ, RS with transversal AC and auxiliary segments for the congruent triangles.
